name: taulman3D
summary: One of the earliest specialty-nylon FDM filament brands, historically based in Missouri, USA, and known for Nylon 645, Nylon 680 FDA, Alloy 910, Nylon Bridge and the T-Glase copolyester line. Acquired by Brazilian petrochemical major Braskem, which now hosts the taulman3D catalog on its braskem3d.com additive-manufacturing portal alongside Braskem's own PP/PE and bio-based filaments.

oem_relationships.notes: Braskem acquired taulman3D outright (Braskem press release; TCT Magazine, announced circa 2021-2022), so this is corporate ownership rather than a supply relationship — 'joint-venture' is the closest available enum value and overstates independence. Braskem's own copy states taulman3D 'is responsible for the entire filament manufacturing process, from raw material to packaging', implying in-house manufacture continued post-acquisition. Not present in research/verified-oem-relationships.md.

Distributor listings (MatterHackers) now show the former taulman3D nylon line under the name Xtellar. The taulman3D-to-Xtellar rebrand is plausible from naming and catalog adjacency but was NOT independently confirmed; flagged for follow-up. Not present in research/verified-oem-relationships.md.

product_lines.name: Nylon 618
product_lines.notes: Nylon co-polymer (PA6-copolymer type) engineered for FDM: low warp, dyeable, bonds to cellulose fibers. A copolymer rather than straight PA6, so mapped to base pa.

product_lines.name: Nylon 645
product_lines.notes: Nylon co-polymer, stiffer and stronger than 618, natural translucent.

product_lines.name: Nylon 680 / Nylon 680 FDA
product_lines.notes: 645-family nylon co-polymer in an FDA-compliant food-contact grade.

product_lines.name: Bridge Nylon (645 Rev B)
product_lines.notes: More flexible revision of 645 at similar strength; same nylon-copolymer family.

product_lines.name: Nylon 230 (n)vent
product_lines.notes: Lower-melt-point nylon copolymer formulated to print on standard brass nozzles without an all-metal hotend.

product_lines.name: Alloy 910 / Nylon 910
product_lines.notes: Alloyed nylon copolymer for high tensile strength, minimal shrinkage and broad chemical resistance; not simply PA6 or PA12.

product_lines.name: T-glase
product_lines.notes: Glycol-modified PET copolyester (PETT): optically clear, low shrinkage, stronger than ABS. Frequently described as PETT/PET rather than strict PETG; mapped to petg on the amorphous-copolyester property profile.

product_lines.name: TECH-G
product_lines.notes: PETG-based grade optimised for large-format prints with low shrinkage.

product_lines.name: PCTPE
product_lines.notes: 'Plasticized Copolyamide TPE' - a nylon/TPE alloy giving a semi-flexible nylon-elastomer hybrid. Neither straight TPU nor straight nylon, so no id fits.

product_lines.name: Carbon-fiber reinforced nylon (braskem3d listing)
product_lines.notes: Listed on braskem3d.com under the taulman3D name; nylon base grade and fiber loading are not stated, so left unmapped.

product_lines.name: T-lyne / Guideline / Enviro PETG
product_lines.notes: Legacy specialty copolyester and monofilament SKUs still carried by distributors; chemistry not confirmed in this research pass, so left unmapped.

additional_notes: Pre-acquisition the company was long associated with St. Peters / O'Fallon, Missouri; that HQ was not re-verified post-Braskem, and it is unclear whether Braskem has since consolidated production into its own Brazilian or US sites. manufacturing_countries is recorded as United States on the strength of the Missouri plant description carried in distributor copy, which may be legacy marketing text. No standalone taulman3d.com was confirmed reachable in this research session — it may now redirect into braskem3d.com — so endpoints.website points at the Braskem AM portal that currently hosts the products. No social profiles were found. No build-plate products found. Offers FDA and medical-grade formulations. Xtellar-labelled SKUs at MatterHackers ranged $16.55-$60.00, but the SKU-level mapping between taulman3D and Xtellar names is unverified.

provenance.conflicts: Brand identity is unresolved: retail listings show the nylon line as 'Xtellar' while Braskem's portal still uses 'taulman3D', and no source confirms the rebrand. Manufacturing location is also unresolved — the Missouri plant claim comes from distributor copy that may predate the Braskem acquisition, and whether Braskem consolidated production into Brazil or its own US sites is unknown. Official website endpoint is an inference (braskem3d.com) because taulman3d.com reachability was not verified.
